name.en-US: Cur Deus Homo? Why God Became Man
name.pt-BR: Por que Deus se fez homem

description.la: Dialogus Anselmi cum Bosone de causa incarnationis et redemptionis: cur Deus homo, in duobus libris. Textus ex editione Migne (Patrologia Latina 158, 1853).
description.en-US: Anselm’s dialogue with the monk Boso on why God became man and how Christ’s death redeems us: the doctrine of satisfaction, in two books. The Latin is the Migne text (Patrologia Latina 158, 1853), from a machine-corrected OCR; the English is Sidney Norton Deane’s 1903 translation, which follows the Latin chapter for chapter (Deane splits Book II chapter XVIII in two, so from there his numbers run one behind the Latin).
description.pt-BR: O diálogo de Anselmo com o monge Bosão sobre a razão pela qual Deus se fez homem e sobre como a morte de Cristo nos redime: a doutrina da satisfação, em dois livros.

sources.edition: S. Anselmi Cantuariensis archiepiscopi opera omnia, ed. J.-P. Migne, Patrologia Latina 158 (Paris 1853), the Gerberon text; TEI XML of the Corpus Corporum (University of Zurich), text 10606, from the Open Greek and Latin machine-corrected OCR.
sources.description: The complete text with its chapter divisions and PL chapter summaries. PL page breaks, the column numbers and the apparatus of alternative chapter numbers (al.) are dropped; Scripture references stay in parentheses as printed. Dialogue turns are set as separate paragraphs. The OCR carries a few residual slips.
sources.tierEvidence: Anselm died in 1109; Migne’s 1853 printing is public domain everywhere.

sources.edition: St. Anselm: Proslogium; Monologium; an Appendix in Behalf of the Fool by Gaunilon; and Cur Deus Homo, translated from the Latin by Sidney Norton Deane (Chicago: Open Court, 1903). Christian Classics Ethereal Library plain-text edition.
sources.description: The Cur Deus Homo only (Deane’s introduction, Gaunilo’s pleading and Anselm’s reply are not imported). Chapter titles are Deane’s chapter headings; translator’s notes are kept as footnotes.
sources.tierEvidence: Published in Chicago in 1903, before 1931: public domain in the US.

title.en-US: Preface

title.la: Liber Primus
title.en-US: Book I

title.la: Caput I. Quaestio de qua totum opus pendet
title.en-US: Chapter I. The question on which the whole work rests

title.la: Caput II. Quomodo accipienda sunt ea quae dicenda sunt
title.en-US: Chapter II. How those things which are to be said should be received

title.la: Caput III. Objectiones infidelium, et responsiones fidelium
title.en-US: Chapter III. Objections of infidels and replies of believers

title.la: Caput IV. Quod hae responsiones videantur infidelibus sine necessitate, et quasi quaedam picturae
title.en-US: Chapter IV. How these things appear not decisive to infidels, and merely like so many pictures

title.la: Caput V. Quod redemptio hominis non potuit fieri per aliam quam per Dei personam
title.en-US: Chapter V. How the redemption of man could not be effected by any other being but God

title.la: Caput VI. Qualiter reprehendant infideles quod dicimus Deum morte sua nos redemisse, et sic dilectionem suam erga nos ostendisse, et pro nobis expugnare diabolum venisse
title.en-US: Chapter VI. How infidels find fault with us for saying that God has redeemed us by his death, and thus has shown his love towards us, and that he came to overcome the devil for us

title.la: Caput VII. Quod nullam diabolus habebat justitiam adversus hominem: et quare videatur habuisse, et cur Deus hoc modo hominem liberaverit
title.en-US: Chapter VII. How the devil had no justice on his side against man; and why it was, that he seemed to have had it, and why God could have freed man in this way

title.la: Caput VIII. Quomodo licet humilia, quae dicimus de Christo, non pertineant ad divinitatem, tamen inconveniens videatur infidelibus ea de illo dici secundum hominem: et unde illis videatur idem homo non sponte mortuus esse
title.en-US: Chapter VIII. How, although the acts of Christ's condescension which we speak of do not belong to his divinity, it yet seems improper to infidels that these things should be said of him even as a man; and why it appears to them that this man did not suffer death of his own will

title.la: Caput IX. Quod sponte mortuus sit; et quid sit, factus est obediens usque ad mortem; et, propter quod Deus illum exaltavit; et, non venit facere voluntatem meam; et, proprio Filio suo non pepercit; et, non sicut ego volo, sed sicut tu vis
title.en-US: Chapter IX. How it was of his own accord that he died, and what this means: "he was made obedient even unto death; " and: "for which cause God hath highly exalted him;" and: "I came not to do my own will; " and: "he spared not his own Son;" and: "not as I will, but as thou wilt."

title.la: Caput X. Item de eisdem; quomodo aliter recte intelligi possunt
title.en-US: Chapter X. Likewise on the same topics; and how otherwise they can be correctly explained

title.la: Caput XI. Quid sit peccare, et pro peccato satisfacere
title.en-US: Chapter XI. What it is to sin, and to make satisfaction for sin

title.la: Caput XII. Utrum sola misericordia, sine omni debiti solutione, deceat Deum peccata dimittere
title.en-US: Chapter XII. Whether it were proper for God to put away sins by compassion alone, without any payment of debt

title.la: Caput XIII. Quod nihil minus sit tolerandum in rerum ordine, quam ut creatura Creatori debitum honorem auferat, et non solvat quod aufert
title.en-US: Chapter XIII. How nothing less was to be endured, in the order of things, than that the creature should take away the honor due the Creator and not restore what he takes away

title.la: Caput XIV. Cujusmodi honor Dei sit poena peccantis
title.en-US: Chapter XIV. How the honor of God exists in the punishment of the wicked

title.la: Caput XV. Si Deus vel ad modicum patiatur honorem suum violari
title.en-US: Chapter XV. Whether God suffers his honor to be violated even in the least degree

title.la: Caput XVI. Ratio cur numerus angelorum, qui ceciderunt restituendus sit de hominibus
title.en-US: Chapter XVI. The reason why the number of angels who fell must be made up from men

title.la: Caput XVII. Quod alii angeli pro illis, non possint restitui
title.en-US: Chapter XVII. How other angels cannot take the place of those who fell

title.la: Caput XVIII. Utrum plures futuri sint sancti homines, quam sint mali angeli
title.en-US: Chapter XVIII. Whether there will be more holy men than evil angels

title.la: Caput XIX. Quod homo non possit salvari sine peccati satisfactione
title.en-US: Chapter XIX. How man cannot be saved without satisfaction for sin

title.la: Caput XX. Quod secundum mensuram peccati oporteat esse satisfactionem; nec eam homo per se facere possit
title.en-US: Chapter XX. That satisfaction ought to be proportionate to guilt; and that man is of himself unable to accomplish this

title.la: Caput XXI. Quanti ponderis sit peccatum
title.en-US: Chapter XXI. How great a burden sin is

title.la: Caput XXII. Quam contumeliam fecit Deo homo, cum se permisit a diabolo vinci; pro qua satisfacere non potest
title.en-US: Chapter XXII. What contempt man brought upon God, when he allowed himself to be conquered by the devil; for which he can make no satisfaction

title.la: Caput XXIII. Quid abstulit Deo cum peccavit, quod reddere nequit
title.en-US: Chapter XXIII. What man took from God by his sin, which he has no power to repay

title.la: Caput XXIV. Quod quandiu homo non reddit Deo quod debet, non possit esse beatus: nec excusetur impotentia
title.en-US: Chapter XXIV. How, as long as man does not restore what he owes God, he cannot be happy, nor is he excused by want of power

title.la: Caput XXV. Quod ex necessitate per Christum salvetur homo
title.en-US: Chapter XXV. How man's salvation by Christ is necessarily possible

title.la: Liber Secundus
title.en-US: Book II

title.la: Caput I. Quod homo a Deo factus sit justus, ut Deo fruendo beatus esset
title.en-US: Chapter I. How man was made holy by God, so as to be happy in the enjoyment of God

title.la: Caput II. Quod homo non moreretur, si non peccasset
title.en-US: Chapter II. How man would never have died, unless he had sinned

title.la: Caput III. Quod cum corpore, in quo vivit in hac vita, homo resurget
title.en-US: Chapter III. How man will rise with the same body which he has in this world

title.la: Caput IV. Quod de humana natura perficiet Deus quod incoepit
title.en-US: Chapter IV. How God will complete, in respect to human nature, what he has begun

title.la: Caput V. Quod quamvis hoc necesse sit fieri, tamen hoc non faciet cogente necessitate: et quae sit necessitas, quae aufert gratiam aut minuit; et quae necessitas augeat
title.en-US: Chapter V. How, although the thing may be necessary, God may not do it by a compulsory necessity; and what is the nature of that necessity which removes or lessens gratitude, and what necessity increases it

title.la: Caput VI. Quod satisfactionem, per quam salvatur homo, non possit facere nisi Deus homo
title.en-US: Chapter VI. How no being, except the God-man, can make the atonement by which man is saved

title.la: Caput VII. Quod necesse sit eumdem ipsum esse perfectum Deum, et perfectum hominem
title.en-US: Chapter VII. How necessary it is for the same being to be perfect God and perfect man

title.la: Caput VIII. Quod ex genere Adae, et de virgine femina Deum oporteat assumere hominem
title.en-US: Chapter VIII. How it behoved God to take a man of the race of Adam, and born of a woman

title.la: Caput IX. Quod necesse sit Verbum solum, et hominem in unam convenire personam
title.en-US: Chapter IX. How of necessity the Word only can unite in one person with man

title.la: Caput X. Quod idem homo non ex debito moriatur: et quomodo possit vel non possit peccare: et cur ille, vel angelus de sua justitia laudandus sit; cum peccare non possint
title.en-US: Chapter X. How this man dies not of debt; and in what sense he can or cannot sin; and how neither he nor an angel deserves praise for their holiness, if it is impossible for them to sin

title.la: Caput XI. Quod moriatur ex sua potestate: et quod mortalitas non pertineat ad puram hominis naturam
title.en-US: Chapter XI. How Christ dies of his own power, and how mortality does not inhere in the essential nature of man

title.la: Caput XII. Quod quamvis incommodorum nostrorum particeps sit, miser tamen non sit
title.en-US: Chapter XII. How, though he share in our weakness, he is not therefore miserable

title.la: Caput XIII. Quod cum aliis infirmitatibus nostris ignorantiam non habeat
title.en-US: Chapter XIII. How, along with our other weaknesses, he does not partake of our ignorance

title.la: Caput XIV. Quomodo mors ejus praevaleat numero et magnitudini peccatorum omnium
title.en-US: Chapter XIV. How his death outweighs the number and greatness of our sins

title.la: Caput XV. Quomodo deleat mors eadem etiam peccata cum perimentium
title.en-US: Chapter XV. How this death removes even the sins of his murderers

title.la: Caput XVI. Qualiter Deus de massa peccatrice assumpsit hominem sine peccato; et de salvatione Adae et Evae
title.en-US: Chapter XVI. How God took that man from a sinful substance, and yet without sin; and of the salvation of Adam and Eve

title.la: Caput XVII. Quomodo non necessitate mortuus est, qui non potuit esse nisi quia erat moriturus
title.en-US: Chapter XVII. How he did not die of necessity, though he could not be born, except as destined to suffer death

title.la: Caput XVIII. Quid in Deo non sit necessitas, vel impossibilitas: et quid sit necessitas cogens, et necessitas non cogens
title.en-US: Chapter XVIII (a). How, with God there is neither necessity nor impossibility, and what is a coercive necessity, and what one that is not so

title.la: Caput XIX. Quomodo vita Christi solvatur Deo pro peccatis hominum: et quomodo Christus debuit et non debuit pati
title.en-US: Chapter XVIII (b). How Christ's life is paid to God for the sins of men, and in what sense Christ ought, and in what sense he ought not, or was not bound, to suffer

title.la: Caput XX. Qua ratione de morte ejus sequatur humana salvatio
title.en-US: Chapter XIX. How human salvation follows upon his death

title.la: Caput XXI. Quam magna, et quam justa sit misericordia Dei
title.en-US: Chapter XX. How great and how just is God's compassion

title.la: Caput XXII. Quod impossibile sit diabolum reconciliari
title.en-US: Chapter XXI. How it is impossible for the devil to be reconciled

title.la: Caput XXIII. Quod in his quae dicta sunt, veritas Veteris et Novi Testamenti probata sit
title.en-US: Chapter XXII. How the truth of the Old and New Testament is shown in the things which have been said
